experiment: E3: prospective, validation-only dispersion selection on real data
question: If an analyst chooses a dispersion option per dataset using validation cells only, how does the choice perform on held-out test cells compared with always using Poisson, always using per-cell dispersion, or the best option in hindsight?
fits: the 24 saved E2 decoders (four encoders x two arms x fit seeds 42-44)
options: per-cell-type (median validation dispersion within type; shared value for types with fewer than 20 validation cells)
selection: within each dataset, the option with the lowest median validation expressed-gene calibration error across the dataset's groups with at least 20 validation cells; ties prefer Poisson, then shared, then per-type, then per-cell; test cells are never used
endpoints: dataset-level median test calibration error of the selected option; regret relative to the best option on test; difference from always-Poisson and always-per-cell; for PCA-512 fits, Welch marker recall of the selected option taken from the matched E1 tables
inference_stats: values averaged over seeds within dataset, then equal-weight over datasets; 2000-resample dataset bootstrap (seed 20261111); selection frequencies by arm
retention: all fits, datasets and options retained
